title: Goods and services in operations

match.reason: The existing goods and services point only defines goods as things you own and services as work done for you, while the new point covers operations ideas like storage, separating production from customers, and producing and consuming at the same time, which is a deeper and different idea for Year 12.

draft.title: Goods and services in operations
card: Goods are physical items, such as a bicycle or a loaf of bread. They can be made in a factory away from customers and stored until they are sold.
Services are actions or experiences, such as a haircut or a dental check-up. They are usually made and used at the same time, so they cannot be stored for later.
Many services need the customer to be present, or to take part. This means the business often has to make the service where the customer is, or when they arrive.
Because goods can be stored, a business can make them ahead of demand. A service business cannot, so it must plan its staff and opening hours to match when customers come.
draft.remember: Goods can be made ahead and stored. Services are usually made as the customer uses them.

a.q: Which feature is most likely to make a service different from a good in operations?
opts: It is usually made and used at the same time
It is made in a factory away from customers
It can be stored until a customer wants it
It is always a physical item that is handed over
a.why: A service is usually made as the customer uses it, so it cannot be stored for later. Storing is a feature of goods, which are physical items and can be made away from customers.
a.clue: Think about whether a haircut can be made and kept on a shelf.

b.q: Tariq runs a bakery in Penrith that sells bread, and a cleaning business that cleans offices at night. Which statement about his operations is correct?
opts: The bread can be baked early and stored for sale
The office cleaning can be done early and stored for later
Both can be stored because both are made by staff
Neither can be stored because both involve labour
b.why: Bread is a good, so it can be made ahead and stored until it is sold. Cleaning is a service, which is made as the customer uses it. Both use staff labour, but that does not decide whether something can be stored.
b.clue: Using staff to make something does not tell you whether it can be stored.

a.best: It is usually made and used at the same time

b.best: The bread can be baked early and stored for sale

problems.detail: Why (b) says cleaning 'is made as the customer uses it', dropping the card's 'usually'. Night office cleaning is also done when the customer is not present, so this wording fits the example loosely and could confuse students about simultaneity.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear right answer. The only issue is minor: why (b) drops the card's 'usually' and loosely describes night office cleaning as made 'as the customer uses it'.
